backend_seam_note: plugins CAN register a TranscriptionProvider, but it is a backend: it is dispatched only when stt.provider names it (built-ins always win) and it must implement speech recognition itself. It cannot borrow the host's configured STT.

builtin_name_rejected.reason: built-in STT names always win; registration is dropped with a warning

builtin_wins_over_plugin.note: stt.provider=local (the default) never reaches a plugin

ctx_has_no_stt_request.note: ctx.register_transcription_provider only installs a backend (Probe B shows what that backend is handed); no ctx member performs a transcription and ctx.rest/ctx.socket are desktop-SDK facades to /api/plugins/<id>, not Python ctx members

ctx_rest_is_namespaced.documented_limit: 'a plugin can't address another plugin's API or a core route through it' (apps/desktop/src/api/plugins.ts:64-70)
ctx_rest_is_namespaced.note: no /api/audio/transcribe reachable through ctx.rest; the route is mounted on the host web app (hermes_cli/web_server.py:825) and its only client auth is the desktop main process bridge

no_transcription_rpc.note: host.request is the gateway JSON-RPC door; it exposes no audio-file -> transcript method

no_transcription_tool.note: ctx.dispatch_tool is a thin wrapper over registry.dispatch (hermes_cli/plugins.py:676)

plugin_provider_dispatch.note: the provider receives the file path and hints ONLY — no stt_config, no credential, no host STT handle. To return a transcript it must run an STT backend itself.

private_import_is_flagged.note: tools.transcription_tools is not on the plugin public-surface allowlist (hermes_cli/plugin_validate_private_imports.py); agent.transcription_provider is

transcribe_audio_end_to_end.note: the seam works only because a fake backend was registered; nothing in this path supplies real speech recognition
